title: The roster of roles that see the other-products account number unmasked is an assumption of the legacy story
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 003 Customer s other products on the case v1.md, sections 3 and 10; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.5; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (masking_rule)
description: The legacy story names the roster that sees v_ace_party_product.account_no clear and marks it assumed: RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL and RW-GUARANT clear, the last four digits for every other role. No FSD, TSD or BRD row fixes that roster for this field, and the masking_rule table carries no seed rows. This story therefore writes the roster as data at masking version MASK-2026.12 and records it as an assumption.
evidence: Legacy section 3: 'The masking rules for v_ace_party_product.account_no are loaded (DL26; assumed: unmasked for RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL and RW-GUARANT, masked to the last four digits for every other role).' Legacy section 10 row 2 carries '(assumed; DL26)'.
proposed: Confirm the five clear roles and that every other role holding Case record R is masked, then load the roster through the masking load path of RWB-P4-AD004-APP.

title: No source fixes the masking version label in force for the wave-2 release, or the rule for two valid versions on one day
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (masking_version, valid_from, valid_to) and T3.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 AC-EXC-P4-004-05 and AC-ALT-P4-004-01 (MASK-SIT-01 example); legacy RWB-E2-003
description: masking_rule is versioned by masking_version with validity dates, but no source names the masking version in force at the 31 December 2026 release: the FSD examples use MASK-SIT-01 for SIT and the matrix uses PM-2026.x. The same silence leaves open which version answers when two rows are valid for the same field and business date. This story uses MASK-2026.12 as the wave-2 label and the latest valid_from on or before the business date as the rule, and the answer always names the version it used.
evidence: TSD P4 T3.1 masking_rule: DF-REF-202 masking_version varchar(20), DF-REF-203 valid_from, DF-REF-204 valid_to; FSD P4 A2.5 example AC uses 'MASK-SIT-01'; no masking version appears in the matrix versions of FSD A2.4 (PM-2026.11, PM-2026.12, PM-2026.13).
proposed: Name the masking version of the wave-2 release in the masking load file and confirm the latest-valid-from rule for a day with two valid versions.

title: No source states whether the other-products account number is the only personal field of the panel
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 003 Customer s other products on the case v1.md, section 11; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.5 field catalogues; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1
description: Legacy section 11 names seven v_ace_party_product fields the panel reads (person_key, account_no, account_key, product_type, product_status, data_as_of, and the customer person_key). Only account_no (DF-ACE-281) has a masking row named, and neither the FSD P4 field catalogues nor TSD P4 T3.1 carry a personal-data classification for the ACE view, so nothing states whether DF-ACE-281 is the only personal field of the panel or that the other six need no row. This story writes rows for DF-ACE-281 only and records the classification as an assumption.
evidence: Legacy section 11 lists DF-ACE-280 to DF-ACE-285 with no personal-data column; FSD P4 field catalogues (A2.1.3.2, A2.3.3.2, A2.4.3.2, A2.30.3.2) cover role and permission fields only and carry a 'Personal data' column that the ACE view fields never appear in.
area: Data classification (P4 rwb-access with P1 rwb-source-data)
owner_role: Data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)
proposed: Record the personal-data classification of the seven v_ace_party_product fields in the data dictionary, and add a masking row or an explicit unmasked false for any further personal field.

title: The field list and the masking step of the gateway-bff composite route for the other-products panel are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (gateway-bff) and DP-19; legacy RWB-E2-003 section 15; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 Screens
description: SCR-03 and its other products panel are served by the gateway-bff composite route, which merges the rwb-integration read with this service's masking answer. No source gives the route's field list, its merge order or where the last-four shape is applied, so the contract between the screen model and this answer is open. This story fixes only the answer shape and leaves the route to its owner.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 20: gateway-bff composes at most a few parallel calls, never calls a service that then calls another; DP-19 names the composite route and RWB-PLT-N001-CON. No route field list appears in FSD P4, TSD P4 T-A or the legacy story.
proposed: Publish the composite route for SCR-03 and its other products panel with its field list and its masking step, under RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

title: It is not settled who writes the PII access event for the composed other-products read
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 003 Customer s other products on the case v1.md, section 4 step 8 and BR5; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T5.1 (INT-22); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 note
description: The legacy story writes one PII access event inside the customer products reader (BR5, INT-22). In the target the read is composed from two services, and Architecture v5 gives audit and PII logging to ACE Common, so the writer is either rwb-integration or the ACE common masking path; no source says which, and the rwb-access slice writes none because DP-03 and DP-09 are not its patterns. The choice does not change this story's answer but it changes who proves TC-E2-003-06.
evidence: Legacy section 4 step 8: 'System: writes one PII access event ... through the ACE PII logging service'; legacy BR5 cites INT-22; TSD P4 T5.1 lists INT-22 as an outbound ACE logging interface; Architecture v5 slide 13 notes that every service writes audit and PII logs to ACE Common.
area: Audit and PII logging (ACE Common, P2 rwb-integration)
proposed: Confirm that the PII access event of the other-products read is written once by rwb-integration through ACE Common on INT-22, and keep rwb-access free of any audit write for this capability.

title: The field names of the masking answer inside the authorise reply and the masking-policies read are not specified
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 Appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (POST /authorise, GET /masking-policies); legacy RWB-E2-003 section 12
description: TSD P4 T-A.1 lists GET /api/recovery/v1/masking-policies with no request or response schema, and describes POST /authorise only through the prose of slide 14; the legacy story describes the masking call as Masking.apply(field, value, roleCodes). No source fixes the field names of the masking answer: the per-role rows, the marker values and the last-four shape. This story states the answer's content and leaves the names to RWB-P4-E1037-CON.
evidence: TSD P4 Appendix T-A.1 lists no row for the masking read and no row for authorise; Architecture v5 slide 14 lists 'POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA) ... /masking-policies' without schemas; legacy section 12 defines String Masking.apply(String field, String value, Set<String> roleCodes) only.
proposed: Fix the masking answer schema in RWB-P4-E1037-CON: the per-role row, the marker values clear and masked, the last-four shape and the masking version.

title: The per-service database login name of rwb-access is not specified
source: DP-02 in the Template and Rules v1 R5.5 table; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (own login per service); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T1
description: DP-02 replaces the shared recovery_svc login with one login per service, and Architecture v5 slide 41 gives each service a schema with its own login, but no source fixes the login name of rwb-access. This story refers to the rwb-access login and names no login string, so no credential or identifier is invented.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02: 'recovery_svc login | One login per service | none'; Architecture v5 slide 41 notes 'schema rwb_<name> in the ACE database with its own login'; TSD P4 T1 names the schema and no login, and TSD P4 T3.1 has no login field.
proposed: Name the rwb_access login in the platform DB story (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON or the P4 DB story) and grant it SELECT on its own schema only.
